title: Federal Rule 23 — class actions
summary: A class action allows named parties to litigate on behalf of an adequately defined group of absent persons when the requirements for representative litigation are satisfied. It can make small claims viable and resolve common issues together.

sections.Role in the course: A class action allows named parties to litigate on behalf of an adequately defined group of absent persons when the requirements for representative litigation are satisfied. It can make small claims viable and resolve common issues together.
sections.What to examine: Identify the class and representatives. Apply Rule 23(a)’s prerequisites and a category under Rule 23(b). Then address notice, opt-out rights, representation, jurisdiction, settlement if proposed, and the scope of any binding judgment.
